expectations.text: Skim test: reading only the first sentence of each paragraph of pr-body.md gives the whole argument (what broke, what changed, what it costs); no first sentence is a qualifier chain or starts with 'Because'.
expectations.evidence: First sentences in order: 'Under gateway trouble, nearly one in ten notifications is lost, and tenants that burst get a wall of 429s every minute.' (what broke) / 'The sender retried three times, one second apart, and only on 5xx' (cause) / 'Retries now back off exponentially and honor Retry-After, and the per-tenant limiter is a token bucket' (what changed) / 'The trade: messages that used to fail fast now wait and get delivered, so the tail latency roughly triples and the worst case grows tenfold.' (cost) / 'Decisions a reviewer should weigh:' / 'Out of scope: ...'. Each review bullet leads with a bold claim or question. No paragraph starts with 'Because'; grep confirms. expectations.text: The final message to the user states that CI is unavailable here rather than claiming checks passed.
expectations.evidence: Final message: 'CI is unavailable in this environment, so the workflow stops here; the swd-submit marker is removed.' Only local make lint/make test results are claimed as green, and the message explicitly discloses that the pre-push gate slipped.

notes: The run is strong on substance (clean commit split, secrets excluded, numbers and trade-offs all present, honest final message) and weak on prose discipline: 24 lint findings, mostly semicolons and 30-40 word paragraph leads in commit bodies, which is exactly what the new writing rules target. Eval critique: assertion 6 ('tests were run and passed before the push') is ambiguous for this run, where an earlier run passed on identical content but the actual pre-push gate reported FAILED and the push went ahead; the eval author should decide whether it means 'some passing run preceded the push' or 'the pre-push check passed and gated the push', and word it accordingly. Assertion 11's 'no file list' is also fuzzy: an 'Other changes' section that names two files with their purpose passes here, but a stricter reading could fail it. No assertion checks that the pushed branch actually passes tests from a fresh clone (I verified this: 7 tests OK), which would have caught a real regression had the stale-pyc failure been genuine. The mermaid diagram in the PR body is neither required nor forbidden; worth deciding whether fenced non-code blocks count as 'pasted code'.
